title: Digital Asset Accounting
answer: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation, token valuation, contract auditing, decentralised treasuries and impairment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the practice of matching on chain transaction records against the balances and entries held in an accounting system.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: Valuing illiquid tokens covers the problem of putting a defensible number on a digital asset that has no reliable market price.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts means reviewing the code that runs on a blockchain to check that it does what its authors claim and nothing more.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recording, measurement and reporting of assets held and controlled by a protocol, a DAO or a similar on chain entity rather than by a conventional company.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers the accounting question of when a non-fungible token, a unique on-chain collectible, or a similar one-of-a-kind digital holding has lost value and must be written down.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting is the work of recording and reporting on blockchain based assets inside a conventional accounting system. In practice, AI is used to pull transaction data from chains, match it against ledger entries, and flag breaks that a person would otherwise hunt through by hand. It also supports valuation models for tokens that rarely trade, and it scans smart contract code for patterns that have preceded losses. The field sits where bookkeeping meets cryptography, and the machine learning is mostly pattern matching and anomaly detection rather than anything exotic.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Reconciliation tools now handle common chains and standard token transfers well, and they cut the manual matching load on high volume wallets. Valuation of illiquid tokens remains contested because a model output is not a market price, and auditors still want observable inputs where they exist. Smart contract auditing has real tooling but no guarantee, since a contract can pass every check and still fail through economic design or key management. Impairment testing for unique digital assets is the least settled area, because fair value is hard to establish when there is no comparable sale. The honest limit across all of it is that the chain record is reliable while the accounting judgement on top of it is not.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation for the base layer, the mechanics of getting on chain events into a general ledger and proving the two agree. Valuing Illiquid Tokens then deals with the hardest input problem, what to do when there is no active market and a model has to stand in for a price. Auditing Smart Contracts covers the code side, what automated review can and cannot establish about a contract before funds move through it. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries extends the same questions to pooled or governed holdings, where control and ownership are spread across parties. Impairment of Unique Digital Assets closes the set by addressing write downs for items that are one of a kind and therefore difficult to benchmark.
